children: Ionis Pharmaceuticals said a key European regulatory committee has recommended expanded approval of its Tryngolza drug for people with severe hypertriglyceridemia.

Ionis on Friday said the recommendation from the European Medicines Agency's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use covers Tryngolza as an adjunct to diet, in combination with other lipid-lowering therapies, for the treatment of adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia.
The European Commission, which generally follows the CHMP's advice, is expected to make a final decision by the end of the year, the Carlsbad, Calif., drugmaker said.
Severe hypertriglyceridemia is commonly defined by very high triglycerides and characterized by an increased risk of acute pancreatitis and other serious health complications.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Tryngolza in June.
